name: Quality Hold
summary: Quality-hold assignment, guided/manual immediate warning dialogs, final pre-save queue confirmation, mock-data-backed restriction metadata, and CRUD operations for QH records.

workflowAreas: Final save confirmation before label queue persistence
userActions: Understand why a quality hold is required
Acknowledge a quality hold immediately when selecting a restricted guided or manual-entry part
Acknowledge the final save-time quality hold warning before data is written to receiving_label_data
Create or update a quality hold record
preserveRules: Keep quality hold business rules unchanged
Keep warning behavior aligned across guided and manual selection flows
Keep the final save-time warning in the shared queue-save path so guided workflow saves cannot bypass it
Keep mock restriction metadata as the source of truth when mock mode is enabled
acceptanceCriteria: Quality hold warnings still appear at the correct time
Guided and manual part selection both trigger immediate warnings for restricted mock parts
Saving to receiving_label_data requires the second quality hold acknowledgment when any load still has an unacknowledged hold
CRUD operations still work for quality hold records
testScenarios: A quality hold warning appears when expected
Selecting the mock part MMFQH0001 in guided or manual flows triggers the warning
Saving a guided workflow session with MMFQH0001 requires the final quality hold confirmation before queue persistence
A quality hold record can be created and updated correctly
validationHints: Confirm warning timing is correct for guided PO selection, manual typed part resolution, and manual PO-part selection
Confirm saving to receiving_label_data is blocked until the second quality hold acknowledgment is confirmed
Confirm mock quality-hold parts are driven by explicit metadata rather than part-number prefix guesses
Confirm CRUD behavior still works correctly
